context: A green suite that has never seen a request from the vendor, because every fixture was invented from prose and the tests build requests the same way the handler consumes them, so handler and fixtures agree with each other and with nothing else. Predicted baseline failure: the agent reviews the diff on its own terms — tidies the switch, adds a couple of negative cases, maybe notes the shared in-memory Map — and never cross-checks a single fixture against the sample delivery sitting in vendor/parcelo-integration-guide.md. Everything that matters is in that mismatch. Parcelo posts application/x-www-form-urlencoded with TitleCase parameters (ShipmentId, TrackingNumber, Status, EventTime); the fixtures are JSON with snake_case keys, so JSON.parse throws on the first real delivery and the endpoint 500s or 400s every event on Friday. The documented Status vocabulary is label_created / in_transit / out_for_delivery / delivered / exception / returned, and the handler switches on created / shipped / failed, of which exactly one documented value, delivered, is handled at all — every other real event hits the default branch and throws. The guide says the signature covers the body exactly as transmitted before any parsing, and verifySignature parses the body to JSON and re-serialises it before hashing, which cannot match a real delivery even once the encoding is fixed. The guide requires rejecting a timestamp more than 300 seconds off, and the handler reads Parcelo-Timestamp only to feed it into the hash, so a captured delivery is replayable forever. And the PR acknowledges 200 before applying anything, catching the failure into console.error, so with retries disarmed by that 200 a thrown update is simply lost — which is how the unknown-status throw becomes silent data loss rather than a retry. The second predicted failure is the fix direction: told not to want more fixtures of the same kind, an agent will still tend to hand-write a corrected set from the parameter table rather than take the sample delivery in the guide verbatim as the seed.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: src/ changed, tests present under test/, and docs/parcelo-go-no-go.md written with an explicit go or no-go. A review write-up with no code or test changes scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: MUST NOT keep or extend the invented payloads
checklist.description: The fixtures MUST NOT remain hand-rolled from the parameter table, and no further invented payloads may be added. The suite is re-seeded from the complete sample delivery in vendor/parcelo-integration-guide.md — its exact parameter names and its exact body string — so that at least one test drives the handler with a body byte-identical to what the guide shows Parcelo sending. Correcting the key names by hand while still constructing bodies from scratch scores at most half. Leaving test/fixtures/tracking-events.js as the source of truth, or adding more entries in its shape, scores zero for this criterion regardless of what else improves.

checklist.name: Signature computed over the transmitted bytes
checklist.description: verifySignature stops parsing and re-serialising the body and hashes the raw request body as received, appended to the delivery id and timestamp. Keeping any JSON.parse / JSON.stringify round-trip, or any other normalisation of the body, inside the signature path scores zero here: it cannot match a real delivery even after the content type is fixed, and the existing tests hide it by re-serialising identically on the way in.

checklist.name: Content type and body encoding corrected
checklist.description: The handler reads application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies as Parcelo sends them, with the documented TitleCase parameters, rather than JSON.parse on the raw body, and a test posts the documented body string under the documented content-type header. Leaving JSON.parse in the handling path scores zero. Parsing the form encoding but then reading snake_case keys off the result scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT acknowledge before the update is durable
checklist.description: MUST NOT leave the pattern where handle returns 200 and then applies the update in a detached queueMicrotask whose failure is swallowed into console.error. A 200 tells Parcelo to stop retrying, so every throw in applyUpdate is a permanently lost event. Either apply the update before responding, or persist the delivery to a durable queue before the 200 and retry it internally, keyed on the stable Parcelo-Delivery-Id. Keeping the detached fire-and-forget scores zero here; moving the work behind an in-process promise or setTimeout with no persistence scores at most half, because it is the same loss with a longer fuse.

checklist.name: Timestamp window added
checklist.description: The handler rejects a delivery whose Parcelo-Timestamp is more than 300 seconds from the receiver's clock, per the guide, with a test proving it. The handler currently reads the timestamp only as hash input, so a captured delivery replays forever; missing this entirely scores zero. Adding the check only in the stale direction, so a future-dated timestamp still passes, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Status vocabulary matched to the documented values
checklist.description: The handler maps the six documented Status values and, per the guide's forward-compatibility rule, acknowledges an unrecognised value instead of throwing on it. Leaving the created / shipped / failed vocabulary in place scores zero. Mapping the six values but keeping the throwing default branch scores at most half, because the guide states new values will be added.

checklist.name: Verdict names what it depends on
checklist.description: docs/parcelo-go-no-go.md gives a straight verdict and states what it rests on — at minimum that nothing here has been confirmed against the sandbox, and that a single real delivery through the sandbox before Friday is what would convert the review into evidence. A verdict of 'go' offered as if the code changes alone settle it scores zero.
